original_question: If X is a smooth Fano threefold with Picard rank rho(X) = 1, must X be K-semistable?
target_in_paper: Problem 10 in §2.1.3 (“Low dimensional cases”): “Any smooth Fano threefold X with ρ(X)=1 is K-semistable.” ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target almost verbatim: it asks about smooth Fano threefolds, imposes Picard number ρ(X)=1, and asks for K-semistability rather than the stronger K-stability or K-polystability. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))
missing_details: Use the paper’s exact universal formulation (“Any ... is K-semistable”) rather than a conditional paraphrase, if the goal is to mirror Problem 10 word-for-word. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))
Spell out that ρ(X) denotes the Picard number of X. The paper states the condition exactly as ρ(X)=1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))

If you want the question fully stand-alone outside the paper, make explicit that X is a smooth Fano threefold, i.e. a smooth projective threefold with -K_X ample. The paper uses this ambient class throughout its discussion of explicit Fano varieties. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))

The nearby context records the present status: the statement is already known except for families No. 1.9 and No. 1.10. That status is not part of the formal question, but it is part of the paper-faithful context. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))

The only explicit equivalent reformulation supplied nearby is valuative: for Δ=0, K-semistability is equivalent to δ(X)≥1, where δ(X)=inf_E A_X(E)/S(E) and the infimum runs over divisors E over X. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))

No ambient ring, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or “for all sufficiently large m” clauses are relevant here. The only implicit setup worth making explicit is the K-stability notion for Fano varieties and, if desired, the ground-field convention. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))
refined_question: Is every smooth Fano threefold X with Picard number ρ(X)=1 K-semistable? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every smooth Fano threefold X with ρ(X)=1, does the stability threshold δ(X)=inf_E A_X(E)/S(E) satisfy δ(X)≥1, where the infimum is taken over all divisors E over X? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))
justification: The draft clearly targets Problem 10 rather than Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3. In §2.1.3 the paper places the question in the low-dimensional classification of smooth Fano threefolds and then states exactly “Any smooth Fano threefold X with ρ(X)=1 is K-semistable,” adding that it is known except for families No. 1.9 and No. 1.10. Theorem 2 gives the paper’s explicit equivalent criterion for K-semistability via the stability threshold δ(X). Earlier in §2, item 5 notes that K-stability and K-polystability do not depend on the ground field, so adding a characteristic-0/algebraically-closed-field convention is only a stand-alone presentation choice, not a change of the paper’s mathematical content. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))
